t: Add _work_queue to WAI-State.json — priority-ordered array with auto-enrollment of new lugs
perceive: 1. Read WAI-Spoke/WAI-State.json — check if _work_queue already exists (it shouldn't). 2. Read templates/commands/wai-lug-schema.md — understand lug types and PEV fields that determine 'ready' status. 3. Read templates/commands/wai-ozi-work-queue-monitor.md — understand current queue monitoring logic.
execute: 1. Add _work_queue schema to WAI-State.json documentation (in wai.md or wai-lug-schema.md): array of {lug_id: string, priority: 1-5, status: 'ready'|'needs_refinement', estimated_steps: int, blockers: string[], enrolled_at: ISO-8601}. 2. Add enrollment rule to wai-lug-schema.md: when a task/bug/feature lug is created with PEV fields, auto-add to _work_queue with status='ready'. Without PEV: status='needs_refinement'. 3. Priority assignment: bugs=1, tasks=2, features=3 (default). User can override. 4. Update templates/spoke/WAI-State.json template to include empty _work_queue: []. 5. Sync all modified files.
verify: 1. WAI-State.json template has _work_queue field. 2. wai-lug-schema.md documents enrollment rules. 3. Creating a task with PEV adds it to queue as 'ready'. 4. Creating a task without PEV adds it as 'needs_refinement'.
acceptance_criteria: _work_queue schema documented in wai-lug-schema.md: {lug_id, priority, status, estimated_steps, blockers, enrolled_at}
Auto-enrollment rule: task/bug/feature with PEV -> ready; without PEV -> needs_refinement
Default priority: bugs=1, tasks=2, features=3 (user overridable)

_behavior_directive.what_this_is: Define the work queue schema and auto-enrollment rules — the data model for priority-ordered work
_behavior_directive.what_this_is_NOT: Not the UI (that's task-work-queue-display-at-wakeup) or chaining (that's task-work-queue-chain-mode)
